main_result: The projection-body volume functional R_d(K)=|ΠK|/|K|^{d-1} is not maximized by simplices in dimension 20. The witness is K=T_10×T_10 with T_10 the standard 10-simplex, and R_20(K)/c_20 = 121·C(20,10)/(21·2^20) = 22355476/22020096 ≈ 1.0152 > 1, where c_d=(d+1)d^d/d!. Corollary: for n≥N, a product of simplices K_n⊂R^n has R_n(K_n)/R_n(T_n) ≥ λ^n for some λ>1, measured relative to the simplex value c_n. I checked the arithmetic (C(20,10)=184756, 121·184756=22355476, 21·2^20=22020096, difference 335380; c_10 = 17187500/567; α = 2^22·5^8/(567·11^9) ≈ 1.2254), the facet formula normalization (cube and simplex checks), the product identity exponents, the simplex value (c_2=6, c_3=18), the zonotope/fiber volume argument, and the Corollary's k/r decomposition and threshold argument. I found no false statement.
proof_strategy: The facet formula h_{ΠP}(u)=½Σ s_F|⟨ν_F,u⟩| (Lemma facets) comes from a double count: each generic line parallel to u meets exactly two facets, and projected facet areas scale by |⟨ν_F,u⟩|, so ΠP is a zonotope of the area-normal vectors s_Fν_F. For products, the facets of A×B are F×B and A×G, which gives Π(A×B)=(|B|ΠA)×(|A|ΠB) and hence R_{r+s}(A×B)=R_r(A)R_s(B). The simplex value comes from the zonotope of the d+1 area-normal vectors of T_d, which is a translate of ([0,1]^d+[0,w])/(d−1)!, with |[0,1]^d+[0,w]|=1+h_{Π[0,1]^d}(w)=d+1 by a fiber/Fubini argument. Affine covariance of R_d is proved for polytopes by tracking normals and areas under L, and extended to general convex bodies by a polytope sandwich and a limit. The main theorem and corollary are then exact arithmetic on c_10^2/c_20 and an exponential comparison using e<11/4.
hardest_part: The general-convex-body limit in Lemma affine (Steps 5–8): the sandwich P_m⊂P⊂μ_mP_m, the passage of projection volumes to the limit, and the claim that the support function of the closure of ∪ΠP_m equals φ. I checked each inequality, but this part relies on several small points stated only in one sentence each. The Lemma facets Step 2 multiplicity argument was the second most delicate, and I verified it as well.

main_result: For d >= 2, a convex body K in R^d has projection body PiK, with support function h(u) = vol_{d-1}(proj_{u-perp} K). The functional R_d(K) = |PiK| / |K|^{d-1} is compared with the simplex value c_d = (d+1)d^d/d!. The main theorem says that K = T_10 x T_10 in R^20 (T_10 the standard 10-simplex) has R_20(K)/c_20 = 121*C(20,10)/(21*2^20) = 22355476/22020096 > 1, so K violates the conjectured bound |PiK| <= c_d |K|^{d-1}. The corollary says that for some lambda > 1 and all large n, some product of simplices K_n in R^n has R_n(K_n)/R_n(T_n) >= lambda^n. I checked the arithmetic: 121*184756 = 22355476, 21*1048576 = 22020096, the difference is 335380, and alpha = 2^22*5^8/(567*11^9) is about 1.2255. I also checked the formula for c_r c_s / c_{r+s} and the cancellation of beta^{10k} in the corollary.
proof_strategy: The facet formula (Lemma facets) writes PiP as a zonotope with one segment per facet, using a Jacobian argument and a count showing a generic line parallel to u meets exactly two facets. For a product of polytopes, the facets of A x B are F x B and A x G, which gives Pi(A x B) = (|B| PiA) x (|A| PiB) and so R is multiplicative (Prop. product). The simplex value is computed from the zonotope: PiT_d is a translate of ([0,1]^d + [0,w])/(d-1)!, and the volume of the extrusion is d+1 by a fiber argument. Affine covariance (Lemma affine) is then used to pass from the standard simplex to all simplices, with a sandwich-by-polytopes argument for general bodies. The theorem and corollary are finite arithmetic on c_d, with a Stirling-type bound c_n < (n+1)(11/4)^n. I followed each step and found no error, though several steps are stated tersely.
hardest_part: The multiplicity count in Step 2 of the facet lemma (Lemma facets), where each generic line through the projection is shown to meet exactly two facets. The argument depends on several small facts: the exceptional set E is null, p lies in the relative interior of exactly one facet, and the open segment between p and q is interior. I checked each of these but several are compressed into one line. The general-body limiting argument (Lemma affine, Steps 5-8) was the next hardest to check, since it relies on the sandwich construction and on the claim that the support functions of the approximants converge.

main_result: For a convex body K in R^d, the projection body ΠK is defined by h_{ΠK}(u)=vol_{d-1}(proj_{u^perp}K). R_d(K)=|ΠK|/|K|^{d-1}, and c_d=(d+1)d^d/d!. The conjectured bound is R_d(K) ≤ c_d for all convex bodies K. The main theorem says that K=T_10×T_10 in R^20 (T_10 the standard 10-simplex) has R_20(K)=c_10^2, and that R_20(K)/c_20 = 121·C(20,10)/(21·2^20) ≈ 1.015 > 1, so the conjecture fails in dimension 20. A corollary gives polytopes K_n in R^n with R_n(K_n)/c_n ≥ λ^n for some λ>1 and all large n. I checked the arithmetic: C(20,10)=184756, 121·184756=22,355,476, 21·2^20=22,020,096, difference 335,380; α=2^22·5^8/(567·11^9)≈1.2255; the bound e<11/4 and c_n<(n+1)(11/4)^n; and the general product formula for c_r c_s/c_{r+s}. All of these are correct.
proof_strategy: The facet formula (Lemma facets) writes ΠP as a zonotope with one segment per facet, spanned by the area-normal vector s_F ν_F. The proof counts that a generic line parallel to u meets the projection of exactly two facets, and double counting gives the factor 1/2. For a Cartesian product, the facets of A×B are F×B and A×G, so their area-normal vectors scale by |B| and |A|. This gives Π(A×B)=(|B|ΠA)×(|A|ΠB), and taking volumes gives R_{r+s}(A×B)=R_r(A)R_s(B). For the standard simplex, the area-normal vectors give ΠT_d as a translate of ([0,1]^d+[0,w])/(d-1)!, and a fiber argument gives the volume d+1, so R_d(T_d)=c_d. Affine covariance is used to extend this to all simplices, and the approximation argument in Lemma affine handles general convex bodies. The main theorem then follows from c_10^2 > c_20 by exact arithmetic. The corollary takes products of many copies of T_10 and bounds c_n by Stirling-type estimates.
hardest_part: The multiplicity-two count in Lemma facets (Step 2) and the limiting approximation argument for general convex bodies in Lemma affine (Steps 5–8). Each step is locally plausible, and I checked the individual inequalities, but the geometric claims about boundary points, faces, and the sandwich ε-approximation are compressed and I could not fully reconstruct every detail from the text alone. I also cannot verify the external literature claims (Chen et al., Feng et al., Henk, Brannen), which the novelty statement depends on.
